neighbours.label: The point where a rate or ratio is being set up: the counted noun or connector just before/at 'for every N', 'X-to-Y ratio', or a statistic about to take 'per' (the pole's output promotes ' per', ' ratio', ' density')
fire: The district employs about four dentists for every ten thousand inhabitants.
In rural areas there is one pharmacy for every 6,000 people.
The survey found 62 mobile phones for every 100 households.
At that college the student-to-faculty ratio is roughly nine to one.
The guard ended the season with 9.3 assists per game, second in the conference.
The island has just two ambulances for every fifty thousand residents.
Inspectors check that the caregiver-to-infant ratio never exceeds one to four.
The county reported 27 bicycles for every 100 commuters last spring.
quiet: The district employs about four dentists at the new health centre.
In rural areas there is one pharmacy and it closes at noon.
The survey found 62 mobile phones left behind in taxis.
At that college the students and faculty share one dining hall.
The guard ended the season with an injury, his second in the conference.
The island has just two ambulances and both are quite old.
Inspectors check that the caregivers wash their hands before feeding.
The county reported 27 bicycles stolen from commuters last spring.

notes: Card: peaks on ' assists', ' staff', 'DP', 'F', ' for', '-to' in per/ratio constructions. Probes: 'beds for every thousand' 0.50, 'doctors for every' 0.41, 'assists per game' 0.30, 'nurse-to-patient' 0.26; plain counts 0.01-0.04. Weaker before a literal 'per' (0.06-0.15).
